o1.biggest_strength: The funnel table by device and browser makes the in-app checkout bug obvious: 4,130 in-app pop-up errors against 4,800 lost in-app carts. It sizes the fix correctly at about 560 orders and ₹34 lakh gross margin a month and ships it first, with an A/A test.
o1.biggest_mistake: It states the smallest detectable effect for each test without showing the working, so I can't check the 10% and 12% figures myself or learn how they were reached.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the sample-size sum once, add stop rules and say how to treat COD orders, so I can trust and reuse the timings.

o2.biggest_strength: It shows the sample-size maths (0.70% baseline, about 227,000 per version for a 10% lift in 4 weeks). It also adds practical safeguards an owner wouldn't know: server-side splitting, stop rules, counting only delivered or prepaid orders for COD, and waiting out the 100-night return window for the firmness test.
o2.biggest_mistake: Test 5 judges a hero-image change on orders at a 10% detectable lift and lists add-to-cart only as a guardrail. Add-to-cart should be the main read for a top-of-page change.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use add-to-cart as the main metric for Test 5, with orders as the guardrail, and add the funnel-rate table by browser so the diagnosis can be seen at a glance.

reason: Both find the in-app bug, value it at ₹34 lakh and rank the same sensible tests. The second shows its sample-size working and adds stop rules, the COD and returns read timing, and the profit caveats, so I learn more and can trust the run times.
